summary: Fix final-review findings: retention ranks by capture time, prunes without holding the backup lock and off the Run loop; S3/SFTP time out on silence only; eject unmounts outside the lock and keeps its new pool ID across retries. API impact: none.

guide.reason: The retention note now states that points are kept by capture time and a late-settling older point is removed by a later backup.

api.reason: No request, response, peer or Controller contract changes; retention, transport timeouts and eject cleanup are internal Core behaviour.

roadmap.reason: Defect fixes in the current backup destination slice.

state.reason: Adds NewPoolID to the ejected host's own pool transfer record in its Core pool peer state, so an interrupted eject resumes with the same new pool identity. It is host-local, not pool-scoped; a fresh Controller adopts the resulting pool from the host as before. The pruning set is in-memory only.
state.record: Pool peer state on the ejected host (poolPeerState.Transfer.NewPoolID); the ejected host recovers it itself on resume, and a Controller reads the resulting pool from that host.

verification.method: Focused go tests for each fix, each shown failing through go test -overlay with the fix reverted (old ranking, lock-held prune, bump-before-delete, write-without-renew S3 conn, old SFTP keepalive timer, per-attempt pool ID, lock-held unmount, unconditional online cleanup), then the full agent and vmhost package tests.
verification.limits: Transport timeouts were not measured on a throttled real link; no lab, NFS, S3 or SFTP service was used. Activation context, retention-note capacity and log suppression have no dedicated tests.
